observed_original_abi.calling_convention_observation: The receiver is read from ECX, copied to ESI at 0x00ae9f57 MOV ESI,ECX and used for every field access. No stack argument is read anywhere in the 169 instructions. The epilogue is a bare RET at 0x00aea166, so the callee pops nothing and the caller owns cleanup. Ghidra's `__fastcall FUN_00ae9f50(int param_1)` is the same one-receiver ECX convention.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: No return value. EAX is a scratch register throughout.
observed_original_abi.termination: two exits, both the same bare RET: 0x00aea166 reached by falling off the end, and 0x00aea15f reached by the null-sub-object jump and by the +0x64 / +0x68 skips.
observed_original_abi.hidden_this_register: ECX is consumed immediately; ESI carries the receiver for the rest of the body, which is what lets ECX be reused as the receiver for the many __thiscall ports.
observed_original_abi.stack_reuse_note: The frame is reused aggressively. [ESP + 0x40] holds 0x3AC86B5 and is also pushed as the first argument of the AppSystem call; [ESP + 0x10] receives 0x13EB90C and is then overwritten with 0x13EB844 before use; [ESP + 0x14] is zeroed by an XCHG with a zeroed EAX. The PUSHes at 0x00ae9f81 and 0x00ae9fd1 are consumed not by the function they precede but by the following RET 0x4 callee, which is why the frame is balanced at every exit.
observed_original_abi.ret_form_evidence: The stack reconstruction was accepted only after reading every callee's last instruction live: 0x00BA9370, 0x00B20750, 0x00B32250, 0x00E14C10 and 0x00BA6D80 end in RET 0x4; 0x00C03260, 0x00F31500, 0x00B3D2A0, 0x00B3D300, 0x00B3D380, 0x00435ED0, 0x00421CF0, 0x00C35240, 0x00A206F0, 0x00BD9BF0, 0x01021090, 0x00DD1CA0 and 0x01021300 end in a bare RET; 0x00AE0930 ends in RET 0x18.

layout.frame: SUB ESP,0x80 then PUSH ESI, PUSH EBX, PUSH EBP, PUSH EDI. 0x80 bytes of locals. Epilogue POP ESI ; ADD ESP,0x80 ; RET. EBX, EBP and EDI are restored by the interior POPs at 0x00aea124..0x00aea126, not by the epilogue, which is why the epilogue pops only ESI.

observed_mechanics: 0x00ae9f50 SUB ESP,0x80 / 0x00ae9f56 PUSH ESI / 0x00ae9f59 CALL 0x00DD1CA0 / 0x00ae9f5e MOV ECX,EAX / 0x00ae9f60 CALL 0x00DD30D0: a two-call prologue that runs BEFORE the guard, and whose result is discarded.
0x00ae9f65 MOV EAX,[ESI + 0x20] / 0x00ae9f68 TEST EAX,EAX / 0x00ae9f6a JZ 0x00aea15f: the entire remaining 500-byte body is guarded on receiver+0x20 being non-null.
0x00ae9f70 CMP dword ptr [EAX + 0xC],0 / 0x00ae9f75 SETZ BL: BL is the polarity bit for the rest of the function. BL == 1 means the sub-object's +0x0C field is ZERO. BL is tested six times.

0x00ae9f7e MOV EAX,[EAX + 0x18] / 0x00ae9f81 PUSH EAX / 0x00ae9f82 CALL 0x00B3D2A0 / 0x00ae9f89 CALL 0x00BA9370: 0x00B3D2A0 ends in a bare RET and consumes nothing, so the pushed key survives and is popped by 0x00BA9370's RET 0x4. The result, EBP, is the profile pointer. On the other branch 0x00ae9f92 XOR EBP,EBP makes it null.

0x00ae9f9c MOV dword ptr [ESP + 0x10],0x13EB90C is superseded thirteen bytes later by 0x00ae9faf MOV dword ptr [ESP + 0x10],0x13EB844. Read live, 0x013EB844 holds 0x004230E0 and 0x013EB90C holds 0x0040FDC0, and 0x004230E0 is a Ghidra function entry with body 0x004230E0..0x0042310D. So this dword is a CODE POINTER, not a data vtable pointer. The first store is dead.
0x00ae9fb7 MOV dword ptr [ESP + 0x48],0 zeroes the last dword of the first record.
0x00ae9fbf MOV EDX,[EDI + 0xC] / 0x00ae9fc2 MOV [ESP + 0x18],EDX: the sub-object's +0x0C value goes into record dword_08.
0x00ae9fc6 TEST BL,BL / 0x00ae9fc8 JZ 0x00ae9fce / 0x00ae9fca MOV EAX,EBP / JMP 0x00ae9fed: on the BL == 0 arm the profile is used directly.

0x00ae9fce..0x00ae9fe8 is the BL != 0 arm: PUSH key / CALL 0x00B3D300 (bare RET, so the key survives) / MOV ECX,EAX / CALL 0x00B20750 (RET 0x4). The 0x00B20750 result is DEAD, because 0x00ae9fde immediately reloads EAX from [EDI + 0x28]. If that is null, 0x00ae9fe5 loads ECX from [EDI + 0x20] and calls 0x00BD9BF0. Reproduced, not tidied.

0x00ae9ff1 MOV EAX,[ESI + 0x20] / 0x00ae9ff4 MOV ECX,EAX / 0x00ae9ff6 TEST BL,BL / 0x00ae9ff8 JNZ 0x00ae9ffd / 0x00ae9ffa MOV ECX,[EAX + 0x20] / 0x00ae9ffd MOV [ESP + 0x28],ECX: when BL == 1 the record's dword_18 keeps ECX, which is the SUB-OBJECT pointer itself rather than a field of it.
0x00ae9ff1..0x00ae9fec for dword_20: TEST BL,BL / JZ take / XOR EAX,EAX / JMP store / MOV EAX,[EAX + 0x24] / store. So BL == 1 stores 0 and BL == 0 stores [EAX + 0x24].

0x00aea010 CALL 0x0067DCC0 is App::IAppSystem::Get per the SDK import. 0x00aea015 MOV EDX,[EAX] / 0x00aea017 MOV EDX,[EDX + 0x14]: vtable slot +0x14. Then PUSH 0 / PUSH &record / PUSH 0x3AC86B5 / MOV ECX,EAX / CALL EDX: three stack arguments, which after cdecl reversal are (0x3AC86B5, &record, 0).
0x00aea02a..0x00aea031 CMP byte ptr [EAX + 0x30],0 / JNZ 0x00aea094: the second record is gated on the sub-object's byte at +0x30 being ZERO.
0x00aea033 CALL 0x01021300 / 0x00aea038 CMP EBP,EAX / JZ 0x00aea094: the second gate is profile != whatever 0x01021300 returns.

0x00aea03c..0x00aea089 builds the second 0x34-byte record with id 0x43F2590, the same code pointer 0x13EB844, dword_08 left UNWRITTEN and dword_10 = EBP, submits it through the same slot +0x14 with the same three-argument shape, then 0x00aea08b LEA ECX,[ESP + 0x50] / 0x00aea08f CALL 0x00421CF0 destroys it immediately. The two record bases, [ESP + 0x10] and [ESP + 0x50], are 0x40 apart, which is what fixes the record size at 0x34 bytes rather than 0x40.
0x00aea094 CALL 0x00B3D380 / TEST EAX,EAX / JZ / PUSH 0x4D02E35 / MOV ECX,EAX / CALL 0x00B32250: 0x00B32250 ends in RET 0x4 and pops the pushed id.

0x00aea0a9 CALL 0x00A206F0 / TEST EAX,EAX / JZ 0x00aea0bd / MOV EDX,[EAX] / MOV ECX,EAX / MOV EAX,[EDX + 0x20] / CALL EAX: the ONLY indirect call in this body, vtable slot +0x20 on the object 0x00A206F0 returns, receiver ECX = that object, result in EAX. 0x00aea0bd XOR EAX,EAX supplies 0 when the object is null. Then PUSH EAX / PUSH 0x1E5E7302 / CALL 0x00435ED0 / ADD ESP,8: a cdecl two-argument publish.

0x00aea0cd CALL 0x00B3D490 (Simulator::cToolManager::Get per the SDK) is called TWICE, at 0x00aea0cd for the null test and at 0x00aea0d6 for the receiver. The second call's result is used, not the first.

0x00aea0e2 PUSH 0x1 / 0x00aea0e4 CALL 0x00B3D400 (bare RET, so the word survives) / MOV ECX,EAX / CALL 0x00E14C10: 0x00E14C10 ends in RET 0x4 and pops it. 0x00B3D400 is Simulator::cGameNounManager::Get per the SDK import.

0x00aea0f0 MOV EAX,[ESI + 0x74] / CMP EAX,-1 / JZ 0x00aea121: the id slot, with -1 as the sentinel. PUSH EAX / CALL 0x00B3D2A0 (bare RET) / MOV ECX,EAX / CALL 0x00BA6D80 (RET 0x4). If the entry exists, CALL 0x01021090 / PUSH EAX / PUSH EDI / CALL 0x00C35240 / ADD ESP,8 binds it. 0x00aea11a then writes -1 back REGARDLESS of whether the entry existed, so the reset is not conditional on the bind.

0x00aea121 MOV ECX,[ESI + 0x64] / POP EDI / POP EBP / POP EBX / 0x00aea127 CMP ECX,dword ptr [ESI + 0x68] / JZ 0x00aea156: +0x64 and +0x68 are compared as two POINTERS, not as a pointer and a cached value of a different type.

0x00aea12c..0x00aea140: four zeros, then 1, then the +0x64 pointer, are pushed and 0x00B3D4D0 (Simulator::cSpaceTrading::Get per the SDK) ignores them because it ends in a bare RET; its result becomes the receiver of 0x00AE0930, which ends in RET 0x18 and pops exactly those six words.

0x00aea145..0x00aea153: the +0x64 versus +0x68 comparison is REPEATED after the release. Only if it still differs is 0x00aea14d MOV byte ptr [EAX],0 executed and +0x68 refreshed from +0x64. The re-check is a real invariant, not a compiler artefact: the release call is allowed to change +0x68.

0x00aea156 LEA ECX,[ESP + 0x4] / 0x00aea15a CALL 0x00421CF0 destroys the first record on the way out. By then the frame has been unwound by the three POPs at 0x00aea124..0x00aea126, so ESP+4 is the first record's base.

sdk_correspondence.caveat: Spore-ModAPI is a third-party clean-room reconstruction, not original EA source and not EA documentation. Where it is cited below it supplies CANDIDATE NAMES only. semantic_contract: A session bring-up routine, entirely guarded on receiver+0x20 being non-null. It first runs two calls whose results it discards. It then builds a 0x34-byte stack record with a code pointer at dword_00, the sub-object's +0x0C at dword_08, a profile pointer at dword_10, and the sub-object's +0x20 or +0x24 at dword_18 and dword_20 depending on whether the sub-object's +0x0C is zero, and submits it to AppSystem vtable slot +0x14 as (0x3AC86B5, &record, 0). If the sub-object's byte at +0x30 is zero and the profile differs from what 0x01021300 returns, it builds and submits a second record under id 0x43F2590 and destroys it immediately. It then sets the flag 0x4D02E35 on the object 0x00B3D380 returns, publishes the result of one virtual call at slot +0x20 on the object 0x00A206F0 returns under the key 0x1E5E7302, resets the tool manager, configures the noun manager with the value 1, resolves the entry named by receiver+0x74 through 0x00BA6D80 and binds it through 0x00C35240, and then writes -1 back to receiver+0x74 whether or not that succeeded. Finally, if receiver+0x64 differs from receiver+0x68 it calls 0x00AE0930 on the space-trading manager, re-tests the pair, and only if it still differs zeroes the byte at *+0x64 and refreshes +0x68 from +0x64. It destroys the first record and returns. It writes three memory locations, all conditional, and saves four registers.
classification_rationale: Not STRONG_SEMANTIC. The complete 169-instruction body, the ABI, the control flow, every constant and every field offset are read directly, and every callee's ret form was read live before the stack reconstruction was accepted. But the fan-out of 23 means the majority of the callees are unresolved: seventeen of the twenty-three are recorded as identified False, and the two vtable targets behind AppSystem slot +0x14 and the foreign slot +0x20 have no resolved concrete callee. The runtime values behind the four hashed ids are not established. Not STRUCTURAL_ONLY, because the guards, the gate polarities, the unconditional +0x74 reset and the double comparison are all behavioural claims that are fully established.
semantic_findings: The whole body is guarded on receiver+0x20 being non-null; a null sub-object runs only the two prologue calls and the epilogue.
0x00ae9f75 SETZ BL inverts the sense of every later test, and the BL == 1 arm stores the sub-object POINTER into the record rather than a field of it.
The record's first dword is a CODE pointer (0x004230E0, a Ghidra function entry), not a data vtable. The neighbouring constant 0x13EB90C is 0x0040FDC0 and the store of it is dead.
The record size is 0x34 bytes, not 0x40: the two record bases are 0x40 apart, so 0x0C bytes of the stride are inter-record padding.
The second record is gated twice: sub->f_30 must be ZERO and the profile must differ from 0x01021300's return. It is destroyed immediately after submission, so the two records do not coexist.
0x00B20750's result is dead on the BL != 0 arm; 0x00ae9fde reloads EAX from [EDI + 0x28] on the next instruction.
receiver+0x74 is reset to -1 unconditionally once the branch is taken, not conditionally on the bind succeeding.
The +0x64 / +0x68 pair is compared TWICE, before and after the release call, and the byte clear and the +0x68 refresh happen only if it still differs. 0x00AEB7B0 re-checks the same pair from outside.
0x00B3D490 and 0x00B3D400 are called through their SDK names; the other 0x00B3D4xx getters in this body are 6-byte anonymous global getters, which is a distinct pattern in the same address range.

Two of the four callers pair this body with an AppSystem submission (0x490D429, 0 and 0x69C3314), so the three ids 0x3AC86B5, 0x43F2590, 0x490D429, 0x69C3314 all reach the same AppSystem slot from this neighbourhood.
unresolved_questions: What are the four hashed ids 0x3AC86B5, 0x43F2590, 0x4D02E35 and 0x1E5E7302? Each is read as an immediate and none is resolved to a property, key, class or enum name.

What is the 0x34-byte record layout, and what do 0x004230E0 and 0x0040FDC0 do when invoked with it? Only the six dwords this function writes are modelled; the rest are left untouched exactly as the original leaves them.

Which AppSystem method is vtable slot +0x14? Ghidra's decompiler calls it `Init`, but the observed three-argument shape (id, record, 0) matches no SDK signature this worker checked, so no name is claimed.
What is the concrete callee behind vtable slot +0x20 on the object 0x00A206F0 returns, and what is its return value used for beyond the 0x1E5E7302 publish?
